subject: Dedicated capacity — mid-term uplift & options for Quantum Retail
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Fiona Chen <fiona.chen@quantumretail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — mid-term uplift & options for Quantum Retail

Hi Fiona,

Thanks again for the session last week — great to see the holiday campaign forecasts. Based on the usage spike in Feb (attached gpu-usage-report.csv) and your Q2 traffic projections, it looks like your Dedicated pool will need additional committed capacity to keep p99 latency within the target and avoid throttling during peak windows.

Quick summary of what we see:
- Current pool: 8x A100 (80GB) reserved for QR production.
- Observed peak queuing at 6–9PM PST; average tail latency creeping up when concurrent batch jobs run.

Two practical ways to proceed; I included the high-level pricing and tradeoffs below and attached an updated SOW draft for the amendment. Please tell me which direction you prefer or if you'd like us to price a hybrid.

Option A — Mid-term uplift (reserved commit increase)
- Add 4x A100 (increase to 12 GPUs reserved).
- Pro-rated billing for the remainder of the existing term, then standard monthly billing on the new commit.
- Throughput guarantee: baseline throughput increase proportional to GPUs; we’ll commit to a 25% improvement to sustained throughput and keep p99 <= 250ms for your current request mix.
- Commercial: we can apply a mid-term uplift discount (details if you want to commit to a 12-month extension).

Option B — Burst + on-demand (no committed uplift)
- Keep current commit; add burstable reserved headroom for peak hours (elastic pool).
- Higher per-minute rate for bursted capacity but no long-term commit.
- Faster time-to-scale, but unit cost higher during peaks; useful if peak is short-lived.

I attached Quantum_Retail_SOW_v2.pdf and the usage report for reference. If you confirm Option A I’ll send the amended SOW and a DocuSign link. If you want numbers, I can run a quick cost comparison for expected token throughput and tail-latency for both options.

Next steps: which option should I price in detail? Happy to jump on a call with Aditya to align on workload patterns.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Quantum_Retail_SOW_v2.pdf (PDF, 235 KB); gpu-usage-report.csv (CSV, 18 KB)
From: Fiona Chen <fiona.chen@quantumretail.com>

Cc: Quantum Retail Procurement <procurement@quantumretail.com>
Date: 2026-03-07T12:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — mid-term uplift & options for Quantum Retail

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks — the report is helpful. A few clarifying Qs before we lock anything down:
1) For Option A, can you share the exact monthly delta (USD) for adding 4x A100s and how prorating will be invoiced mid-term?
2) What kind of SLA/throughput guarantees come with the increased commit? We need to preserve our customer-facing 99.9% availability and avoid latency regressions during checkout flows.
3) If we do Option B, what is the effective cost per peak hour compared to Option A? We want a clear TCO for both.

If you can include a simple 12-month vs remaining-term cost table that shows net savings and effective discount, that’ll make procurement happy.

—Fiona
Head of Platform Engineering | Quantum Retail
fiona.chen@quantumretail.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — mid-term uplift & options for Quantum Retail

Hi Fiona — thanks for the questions. Below are the concrete numbers and a simple cost table so procurement can compare. I also call out the operational guarantees.

Assumptions: current term ends 2026-09-30; existing commit: 8x A100 (80GB) at list rate $13,200/GPU/month (example list for illustration).

Option A — Add 4x A100 (reserved uplift to 12 GPUs)
- Pro-rated uplift for remainder of term (Mar 9 — Sep 30): 4 GPUs * $13,200 * 6.72 months = $355,000 (approx).
- Ongoing monthly after term reset (if you renew at 12 GPUs): 12 * $13,200 = $158,400/month.
- Discounting: mid-term uplift discount available now: 12% off list on the additional capacity if you accept the amendment within 7 business days. If you instead sign a 12-month renewal for the whole pool we can extend to 18% off list across the 12 GPUs.
- SLOs: we’ll include a throughput guarantee in the SOW for steady-state traffic — target is +25% sustained throughput vs current commit and p99 latency <= 250ms based on current request mix. We’ll also add a rollback/fallback policy to reduce capacity if a regression is detected during a one-week canary.

Option B — Burstable elastic pool (no commit increase)
- Keep 8 GPUs committed; add 6 GPUs of hourly burst capacity available during peaks.
- Burst rate (hourly equivalent) = $18,000/GPU/month (blended on-demand rate); we bill only minutes used.
- Example for 200 peak-hours/mo: estimated burst spend = (6 GPUs * $18,000/12 * 200/ (24*30)) ~ $60,000/month in peak usage.
- Pros: immediate relief, no multi-month financial commitment. Cons: higher unit cost and less predictable monthly total.

Simple 6-month delta (illustrative)
- Option A (pro-rated + monthly after term reset): ~ $355k pro-rated now + lower predictable monthly after renewal; effective unit cost with 12% uplift discount reduces incremental GPU cost to ~$11,616/GPU/month.
- Option B (estimated peak-driven spend): ~ $60k/month during peak months, less predictable.

Attachments: I updated the SOW (see attached) with the SLO language and an amendment template for the pro-rated uplift. If you want, I’ll prepare two SOWs: (1) amendment + 12% mid-term uplift discount, (2) full 12-month renewal at 18% off.

If procurement wants a 15% midpoint discount, we can escalate to finance for an approval — I’ll loop Rishi to confirm.

Happy to review the numbers on a quick call today or tomorrow.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Quantum_Retail_SOW_v2.pdf
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-03-09T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal — quick approval for a 15% uplift discount?

Rishi / Aditya,

Looping you in — Quantum Retail is leaning toward Option A (add 4 GPUs) but procurement just asked for 15% off the incremental capacity instead of the 12% I quoted. Deal details: mid-term pro-rated uplift (~$355k) + potential 12-month renewal conversation.

Can we approve a 15% discount on the incremental capacity for a signed amendment this week? If not, what’s the max we can offer without an exec sign-off? I can push for the 12% now but need to know if we have room.

Thanks — will hold the DocuSign step until I have your go-ahead.

—Vanessa
From: Fiona Chen <fiona.chen@quantumretail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Quantum Retail Procurement <procurement@quantumretail.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — mid-term uplift & options for Quantum Retail

Vanessa — appreciate the clear options and the table. Procurement ran the numbers and here’s where we landed:

We are prepared to sign the mid-term uplift (Option A) if Redwood can meet a 15% discount on the incremental 4 GPUs and include the SLO language described (p99 <= 250ms; +25% sustained throughput; rollback policy). We prefer a DocuSign amendment to the existing SOW and a single invoice that shows the pro-rated uplift line item.

If you can send the amended SOW + DocuSign link with those terms I’ll route for signature on our side today.

Thanks,
Fiona Chen
Head of Platform Engineering | Quantum Retail
